definitions.explanation: A temperature that is notably high. Used in weather reports, cooking, science, and safety warnings. The opposite is {低温|ていおん}.

examples.japanese: {今日|きょう}は{高温|こうおん}{注意報|ちゅういほう}が{出|で}ている。
examples.english: A high temperature warning has been issued today.

examples.japanese: {高温|こうおん}で{焼|や}くとパリッと{仕上|しあ}がる。
examples.english: Baking at high temperature gives a crispy finish.

examples.japanese: {高温|こうおん}{多湿|たしつ}の{環境|かんきょう}では{食品|しょくひん}が{傷|いた}みやすいので、{冷蔵庫|れいぞうこ}で{保管|ほかん}してください。
examples.english: Food spoils easily in hot and humid conditions, so please store it in the refrigerator.

notes:
Compound of {高|こう} (high) + {温|おん} (temperature). Very common in weather reports, product labels, and safety instructions.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {高温|こうおん}{多湿|たしつ} (hot and humid)
- {高温|こうおん}{注意報|ちゅういほう} (high temperature warning)
- {高温|こうおん}で{焼|や}く (bake at high temperature)
- {高温|こうおん}に{注意|ちゅうい} (caution: high temperature)
- {高温|こうおん}{殺菌|さっきん} (high-temperature sterilization)

SIMILAR WORDS:
The opposite is {低温|ていおん} (low temperature). {猛暑|もうしょ} (extreme heat) specifically refers to weather, while {高温|こうおん} is used more broadly for any context involving high temperature.
